academy.label: The Academy
academy.title: Capoeira4Life in London
academy.lead: Real capoeira in a welcoming gym space, with specialized masters guiding every roda.
academy.imageAlt: Capoeira classes at the Capoeira4Life academy in London
body: Capoeira4Life offers regular classes at our academy in London, open to beginners and experienced capoeiristas. Capoeira is taught with respect for its Afro-Brazilian roots, combining movement, music, culture and community.
Our masters specialize in technique, musicality, children's capoeira, fitness and the traditions of Capoeira Nagô. Each brings years of experience to help you grow at your own pace.
Whether you are starting out, training conditioning, connecting with Brazilian culture or trying something new, there is a place for you in our roda.

nago.label: Our group
nago.title: Capoeira Nagô
nago.lead: Preserving Afro-Brazilian traditions and taking capoeira to the world since 2002.
nago.body: Founded in Goiânia by Mestre Pequinês with support from Mestre Suíno, Capoeira Nagô Sports Association honours the Yoruba roots of the art. The name "Nagô" references the African peoples who shaped capoeira in Brazil. Today the group is present across Brazil and internationally, balancing high-performance sport with music, mutual respect and social inclusion.

founder.label: Founder
founder.name: Mestre Pequinês
founder.text: Mestre Pequinês founded Capoeira Nagô in 2002 with a mission to keep ancestral roots alive while transforming lives through capoeira. His social work reaches over 1,500 children in vulnerable communities, using the art as a tool for education, inclusion and citizenship.

cords.label: Graduation
cords.title: Cord Exchange
cords.lead: In capoeira, a student's progress is marked by cords: woven ropes that symbolise level of knowledge, responsibility and dedication to the art.
body: Unlike other martial arts, capoeira uses cords rather than rigid belts. Each colour represents a stage on the capoeirista's journey, from beginner student to master. In Capoeira Nagô, the official system includes specific paths for adults, children (5 to 10 years) and youth (11 to 14 years), as shown in the chart.

A cord exchange is not based on training time alone. The master or teacher evaluates technical growth, musicality, knowledge of history and rituals, behaviour inside and outside the roda, and respect for tradition. Each student progresses at their own pace.

The exchange ceremony is both festive and solemn: family, friends and the whole roda come together. The capoeirista plays, sings and demonstrates what they have learned. Receiving a new cord also means taking on new responsibilities within the group.

steps.title: Evaluation by the master
steps.text: Technique, musicality, conduct and cultural knowledge are assessed before each exchange.

steps.title: Ceremony in the roda
steps.text: The new cord is given at a collective event, with games, songs and community celebration.

intro.label: Capoeira4Life Project
intro.title: O Capoeirinha
intro.lead: Capoeira for the little ones: fun, movement and culture from an early age.
intro.body: O Capoeirinha is a Capoeira4Life initiative created to introduce children to capoeira in a playful, safe and inspiring way. Through games, music and movement, kids learn coordination, respect, confidence and the rich cultural roots of this Brazilian art, all while having fun.

about.label: The project
about.title: Meet O Capoeirinha
about.avatarText: O Capoeirinha is our friendly mascot: a young capoeirista who guides children through every move, making learning feel like an adventure. Colourful, energetic and full of personality, he represents the joy and freedom that capoeira brings to kids.

moves.label: Learn
moves.title: Capoeira Moves
moves.subtitle: Swipe through the moves and learn with O Capoeirinha

items.name: Ginga
items.description: The base movement of capoeira: a rhythmic sway from side to side that teaches balance, flow and readiness for any move.

items.name: Au
items.description: A cartwheel performed with open arms. It develops coordination, spatial awareness and the courage to move freely.

items.name: Macaquinho
items.description: A low move close to the ground, like a little monkey. Builds agility, arm strength and playful movement.

items.name: Negativa
items.description: A low defensive escape with hands on the ground. Teaches protection, reflexes and how to dodge with cunning.

items.name: Ponte
items.description: A bridge with the body arched upward. Strengthens arms, legs and spine. A fun challenge for the little ones!

graduation.label: Graduations
graduation.title: Cords for Children & Teens
graduation.lead: Graduation in Capoeirinha celebrates effort, technical growth and respect for capoeira culture.
body: Children and teenagers earn cords as they progress in class. Each colour marks a stage of learning, from first steps to more advanced movements.
Evaluations consider participation, respect, musicality and mastery of fundamentals, not just physical ability. Every child grows at their own pace.
Teens follow a progressive path that prepares them for the adult graduation system, keeping the same values of discipline and cultural identity.

steps.title: Progressive evolution
steps.text: Each cord represents a new challenge conquered with dedication in class.

steps.title: Fair criteria
steps.text: Behaviour, attendance and love for capoeira count as much as technique.

steps.title: Celebration ritual
steps.text: Graduation ceremonies are festive moments with family, friends and the whole roda.

history.label: History
history.title: Capoeira
history.lead: A martial art, dance and culture born from the resistance of African peoples in Brazil.
history.body: Created during the colonial period as a form of physical and cultural resistance, capoeira disguised fighting moves with music, dance and rhythm to evade surveillance on the plantations. Banned after abolition in 1888, it was only legitimised in the 1930s, when Mestre Bimba founded Capoeira Regional and Mestre Pastinha codified Capoeira Angola. In 2014, UNESCO recognised the Capoeira Circle as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
history.imageAlt: Capoeira roda with practitioners in motion

masters.label: Legacy
masters.title: Pioneer Masters
masters.bimbaText: Mestre Bimba revolutionised the art by creating Capoeira Regional in the 1930s. He transformed the practice into a disciplined method of self-defence, introducing white uniforms, strict rules and the first teaching methodology. In 1937, after performing for President Getúlio Vargas, he legalised capoeira as a national sport. His style is marked by a fast, upright, athletic game focused on the efficiency of strikes.
masters.bimbaImageAlt: Mestre Bimba, creator of Capoeira Regional
masters.pastinhaText: Mestre Pastinha became the great guardian of Capoeira Angola, the traditional style. In 1941, he founded his official school to preserve the African roots, ritual and philosophy of the art. He believed capoeira was a dance of cunning and strategy, played more slowly, rhythmically and close to the ground. He also standardised his students' uniforms in black and yellow.
masters.pastinhaImageAlt: Mestre Pastinha, guardian of Capoeira Angola
